resolution.rationale: CT-79 rejects the original Docker/PostgreSQL fit assumption for v0.1; the old capability evidence remains historical and no longer blocks the accepted local-runtime direction.

evidence.ref: Sponsor goal in the current Codex task, received 2026-08-19
evidence.claim_supported: The sponsor requires a free open-source, self-hostable core Linear replacement with high interaction fidelity and local Control Tower tracking.
The authenticated reference projects view uses dense rows, inline metadata, progress, and a contextual summary surface.
The authenticated reference issue view uses compact grouped rows and configurable visible properties.
The authenticated project overview integrates project properties, resources, milestones, progress, and activity.
The authenticated issue detail integrates rich description, properties, milestone and project context, relations, comments, and activity.
Linear documents projects as units for planned work with properties, views, and progress behavior.
Linear documents a project overview surface combining project information and work context.
Linear documents milestones as project-stage containers for issues with progress.
Linear documents issue creation through multiple contextual and keyboard-aware paths.
Linear documents configurable grouping, ordering, filtering, and visible properties for work views.
Plane is an open-source project-management substitute covering work items, cycles, modules, views, pages, and analytics.
OpenProject is an open-source substitute with broad project, agile, collaboration, time, and cost capabilities.
Taiga is an open-source agile project-management substitute.
Vikunja is an open-source self-hostable task-management substitute emphasizing data ownership.
Playwright supports deterministic screenshot comparison with configurable pixel-difference thresholds.
PostgreSQL supports row security policies that can restrict rows per user or role under a default-deny model.
PostgreSQL includes full-text search facilities suitable for an initial self-hosted search boundary.
WCAG 2.2 defines testable accessibility success criteria for the web product.
The repository contained no runnable product, so new-product capability baselines were zero at bootstrap.

Stack Overflow's 2025 survey covers more than 49,000 developers in 177 countries and reports large question-level samples for collaboration-tool use, work and personal tool counts, and technology adoption or rejection factors.
PMI's 2024 report covers 2,246 project professionals and 342 leaders worldwide across industries and reports material predictive, hybrid, and agile method use.
GitLab and Omdia surveyed more than 5,000 DevSecOps professionals in 39 countries; 64 percent wanted toolchain consolidation and 67 percent reported mostly or completely automated lifecycles.
Atlassian's 2024 survey covers 5,000 knowledge workers across work management, ITSM, and DevOps and reports material goal, tracking-consistency, duplication, and information-retrieval friction.
Node 24.18 provides a file-backed synchronous SQLite API with foreign-key, defensive-mode, busy-timeout, prepared-statement, and online-backup controls behind a release-candidate stability label.
SQLite documents local application storage, application-file use, serialized server requests, and single-writer workloads as appropriate uses.
SQLite documents an online backup API that can copy a consistent snapshot while the source remains available, subject to explicit locking and error handling.

external_research.rationale: Official product and technical sources were reviewed on 2026-08-19. On 2026-08-21, CT-77 added four official large-sample statistical sources and CT-79 added the official Node and SQLite sources supporting the local-runtime architecture amendment.

questions.gap: CT-77 ranks migration-critical workflow families, but the prevalence and effort of exact legacy import formats remain unmeasured.

tasks.description: Synthesize current official large-sample online statistics across varied project types and rank migration-critical workflow families with labeled limitations and sensitivity checks.
tasks.deliverable: A source register, extracted-statistics table, reproducible scoring model, ranked workflow decision, revised traceability, and validator readback.

tasks.description: Measure eight matched, non-destructive reference workflows for median completion time, interaction count, errors, and recovery behavior.
tasks.measurement_method: Repeat each scripted workflow three times after one warm-up in authenticated Chrome with fixed viewport, synthetic or non-submitted content, and explicit start/end rules.
tasks.data_source: Authenticated Linear Chrome observations plus timestamped measurement worksheet; no Linear API, MCP, or provider mutation.
tasks.deliverable: A versioned benchmark specification and verified per-task baseline table with environment, timing, interactions, errors, and artifact paths.

tasks.owner: Product owner and qualified legal reviewer
tasks.description: Select the public license and name and define the clean-room, asset, copy, trademark, and evidence-publication boundary.
tasks.deliverable: An accepted license/name decision, clean-room policy, dependency-license policy, asset provenance template, and pre-release review owner.

tasks.description: Prototype two-workspace isolation, dense issue interaction at seeded scale, deterministic visual tests, and migration/restart recovery.
tasks.deliverable: Disposable prototype evidence with commands, source revision, environment, measurements, failures, and architecture recommendation.

tasks.description: Produce the accepted Sprint Planning document family and executable issue graph from the validated Discovery package.
tasks.deliverable: Accepted PRD, architecture, UX, risk, acceptance, test, deployment, observability, and planning handoff artifacts with exact outcome contracts.

tasks.description: Review the Docker and PostgreSQL footprint and replace it with a bounded local-first architecture for the accepted personal-use scope.
tasks.deliverable: A repository inventory, option comparison, accepted Node and SQLite decision, non-destructive migration plan, test boundary, and replacement issue topology.

tasks.description: Verify that the implemented one-process SQLite runtime satisfies the accepted personal workload, local-security, migration, recovery, and offline boundaries.
tasks.deliverable: Independent clean local start, upgrade, backup, restore, rollback, canonical source import, accepted-scale scan/search/sort, interruption, and outbound-denied evidence.

outcomes.subject: target_user
outcomes.target_segment_or_system: the configured technical owner using the supported single workspace and single team
outcomes.expected_change: complete the bounded project, milestone, and issue workflow on a self-hosted release without facilitation or a critical error

metric.name: core workflow completion rate
metric.definition: share of ten independently reset canonical runs completing local-runtime entry, project and milestone planning, issue execution, saved view, context-preserving detail edit, and persisted readback
metric.workload: ten independently reset canonical seeded core workflow runs

measurement.method: instrumented owner workflow runs with fixed task definitions, independent seed resets, and synthetic data
measurement.source: versioned owner-run observation records and application audit evidence

guardrails.name: unauthorized local data access count
guardrails.metric_definition: count of confirmed events where a remote listener, hostile browser origin, or unsafe local path exposes or mutates product data
guardrails.source: local-origin, listener, filesystem, import security tests and confirmed incident records

invalidation_threshold.metric_definition: core workflow completion rate after two bounded remediation rounds

assumptions: CT-77's statistical ranking keeps the canonical workflow migration-critical across supported project types
the supported one-process local runtime and accepted personal workload remain stable

outcomes.subject: target_user
outcomes.target_segment_or_system: the configured technical owner completing matched core tasks in OpenLinear and the approved reference condition
outcomes.expected_change: complete the matched workflow with near-reference time and interaction cost

metric.name: median reference-relative task-time overhead
metric.definition: median across approved tasks of one hundred times OpenLinear median completion time divided by Linear median completion time minus one hundred
metric.population: the configured owner across repeated task attempts in both matched conditions
metric.workload: eight approved project, milestone, issue, view, and detail tasks

measurement.method: matched-task timing study by the configured owner with fixed viewport, start and end rules, warm-up, repetitions, and interaction-count diagnostic
measurement.source: CT-2 benchmark worksheet and corresponding OpenLinear test-run records

guardrails.name: matched-task error rate
guardrails.metric_definition: share of measured task attempts ending in an unrecovered user or product error

invalidation_threshold.metric_definition: median reference-relative task-time overhead after two bounded interaction revisions

assumptions: matched task definitions remain behaviorally equivalent
approved reference evidence remains admissible after qualified clean-room review

outcomes.subject: protected_quality
outcomes.target_segment_or_system: approved clean-room project, milestone, issue-list, and issue-detail fixtures at pinned viewports
outcomes.expected_change: preserve the reference workflow's structural density and spatial hierarchy with independently designed identity

metric.name: worst-fixture structural screenshot difference
metric.definition: maximum approved-fixture share of comparable unmasked pixels differing beyond the per-pixel tolerance in the pinned environment
metric.workload: one deterministic capture per approved screen and viewport

measurement.method: Playwright screenshot comparison with pinned browser, fonts, viewport, fixture, locale, time, and motion
measurement.source: versioned clean-room visual baselines and CI comparison artifacts

guardrails.name: serious automated accessibility violations
guardrails.metric_definition: count of serious or critical automated accessibility violations on core screens

invalidation_threshold.metric_definition: worst-fixture structural screenshot difference after two bounded visual revisions

assumptions: the pinned rendering environment is reproducible
clean-room masks exclude only branding and documented volatile regions

outcomes.subject: system
outcomes.target_segment_or_system: supported one-process local releases using the canonical seeded dataset and SQLite upgrade path
outcomes.expected_change: preserve all authoritative local records through export, SQLite backup, restore, upgrade, rollback, and compatible import

metric.name: authoritative data round-trip success rate
metric.definition: share of export-import and backup-restore trials whose canonical record and relation digest matches the source
metric.population: supported operating-system, pinned-Node, and schema-version combinations in the release matrix
metric.workload: one canonical export-import and one backup-restore trial per supported combination

measurement.method: canonical export digest comparison across export-import, backup-restore, restart, and accepted upgrade trials
measurement.source: versioned recovery test artifacts and canonical digests

guardrails.name: critical data-loss defect count
guardrails.metric_definition: count of confirmed critical defects that irreversibly lose an authoritative record in a supported operation
guardrails.source: recovery tests and confirmed defect records

invalidation_threshold.metric_definition: authoritative data round-trip success rate on the release candidate

assumptions: canonical serialization covers every authoritative record and relation
supported runtime and schema combinations are frozen before review

outcomes.subject: protected_quality
outcomes.target_segment_or_system: complete public source, build output, local runtime artifact, documentation, assets, and release manifest
outcomes.expected_change: be publishable under an accepted open-source license with distinct identity, complete provenance, and no private reference material

metric.name: mandatory clean-room release audit pass rate
metric.definition: share of mandatory identity, license, attribution, asset provenance, private-evidence exclusion, and reproducible-build checks passing
metric.population: mandatory checks in the accepted public-release audit matrix
metric.workload: one complete audit of the release candidate and its source distribution

measurement.method: manifest, provenance, license, private-evidence, identity, and reproducible-build audit by assigned reviewers
measurement.source: signed release audit matrix and build manifest
measurement.owner: Product owner and qualified release reviewers

guardrails.name: private authenticated reference artifacts in distribution
guardrails.metric_definition: count of private authenticated screenshots, raw workspace records, tokens, or equivalent reference artifacts found in the public distribution
guardrails.source: release privacy scan and provenance audit

invalidation_threshold.metric_definition: mandatory clean-room release audit pass rate at the release decision

assumptions: the final public name and license are accepted before publication

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: A fresh supported user account starts the loopback application without login, Docker, a database server, or an external identity provider and reads the same owner data after restart.
requirements.planned_validation_method: clean local start, origin-security, and restart end-to-end tests

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: First start automatically provisions one owner profile, internal workspace and team identifiers, and statuses that read back after restart while administration and switching controls remain absent.
requirements.planned_validation_method: domain, API, restart, canonical-transfer, and supported-surface end-to-end tests

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: Project state and derived progress survive refresh, filtering, archive, and restore.
Reordering and issue state changes produce deterministic milestone progress.
Keyboard and contextual issue creation persist supported core fields under a stable identifier and implicit owner context without a non-owner assignee control.
requirements.planned_validation_method: issue API, keyboard, supported-property, and end-to-end tests

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: Valid inverse relations persist and invalid self-relations are rejected.
Each accepted issue or project mutation records actor, time, field, and before and after semantics.
A personal saved grouped view restores the same query and presentation state without a sharing-scope control.
requirements.planned_validation_method: saved-view contract and browser end-to-end tests

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: Identifier, title, description, label, and project search returns deterministic bounded results inside the accepted personal workload without a search service or scale index.
requirements.planned_validation_method: bounded-scan relevance, deterministic sorting, and accepted-workload tests

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: Every approved core action is reachable without a pointer and supports Escape recovery.
requirements.planned_validation_method: keyboard matrix and matched-task timing study

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: Closing details restores list filters, scroll position, selection, and focus.
Routine deletion can be restored and irreversible purge requires explicit elevated confirmation.
A versioned round trip preserves every authoritative record and relation digest.
A clean supported user account reaches a healthy loopback application with one command, no Docker or database server, and survives restart and a tested SQLite upgrade.
requirements.planned_validation_method: CT-82 clean local install, migration, restart, and rollback rehearsal

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: The release audit finds no private reference artifact or unapproved identity element.
requirements.planned_validation_method: asset provenance and clean-room release audit

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: Remote listeners, hostile browser origins, unsafe data paths, symlinks, and corrupt imports cannot expose or mutate local product data.
requirements.planned_validation_method: loopback listener, Host/Origin/CSRF, path, permission, and import adversarial suite

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: Serialized writes, revisions, and bounded retries surface stale conflicts and never silently replace committed state.
requirements.planned_validation_method: single-process concurrency, revision, busy-timeout, and request-replay tests

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: The fixed seeded workload remains inside the Planning-approved p75 interaction and render budget.
Core workflows have visible focus, valid semantics, and no serious automated accessibility violation.
requirements.planned_validation_method: axe, accessibility snapshots, keyboard, and manual assistive-technology review

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: Approved fixtures remain within accepted per-screen structural screenshot thresholds.
Failure injection yields actionable non-sensitive diagnostics and correct health state.
A verified SQLite online backup and restored canonical export match the pre-backup record and relation digest while the last known-good file remains recoverable.
requirements.planned_validation_method: online backup, integrity, canonical digest, restore, interruption, and rollback comparison

requirements.acceptance_criterion_placeholder: The source-release manifest contains build, license, attribution, contribution, and security artifacts.
A network-denied one-process local runtime completes the core workflow and backup without Linear, Google, Docker, a database server, or paid services.
Approved desktop, tablet, and mobile matrices keep all core controls and text usable without overlap.
